clue.text: Macho man embraces something irrational and dumb

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold in one's arms, so the first piece wraps round the second

blocks.note: a stud is a virile, macho man
pi is the best-known irrational number

explanation.surface: A tough guy is wrapped up in some senseless, foolish notion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Irrational' reads as a judgement of behaviour, but here it is mathematical: pi cannot be written as a fraction.
explanation.definitionFit: Dumb in its informal sense means lacking intelligence, which is a synonym of the answer.

clue.text: 'Bird' found in 'White Album'

indicators.note: something found in a title is sitting inside its letters, spanning the two words

blocks.note: the end of the first word runs into the start of the second

explanation.surface: A Beatles track called 'Bird' supposedly turns up on the White Album.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make both look like song and record titles; the White Album is the Beatles' 1968 double album.
explanation.definitionFit: A teal is a small freshwater duck, so it is an example of a bird.

clue.text: Rogue cop seen in Christmas décor

indicators.note: a rogue has gone wrong and off the rails, so the letters that follow are disordered

blocks.note: all nine letters are used

explanation.surface: A crooked policeman is spotted among the festive decorations.
explanation.definitionFit: The cones of conifers are often gilded or left plain and hung as seasonal ornaments, so they count as holiday decoration.

clue.text: Forlorn, hollow dummy covers behind

indicators.note: a hollow word has had its insides scooped out, leaving only its outside letters
a cover goes round something, so the outer pair wraps round the next piece

blocks.note: just the first and last letters
behind as a noun is the backside, the rear

explanation.surface: A sad, empty-headed mannequin hides its bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: Forlorn and dreary both describe a bleak, gloomy, cheerless state, so they work as synonyms.

clue.text: Well off, but bound by summons to where convict marks time

indicators.note: off as in gone bad or out of order, so the preceding word's letters are rearranged
something bound by another is tied up inside it

blocks.note: the word itself, to be rearranged
a call is a summons

explanation.surface: A rich man ends up summoned to court and sent to prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Well off' reads as wealthy, but 'off' is the anagram signal for the word before it, and the jumble goes inside CALL after its C.
explanation.definitionFit: A prisoner counting days traditionally scratches tally marks on the wall of the room where he is locked up.

clue.text: Strangely, casual attire on you at first elicits words of warning

indicators.note: something done strangely is done oddly, so the letters come out in an unusual order
at first points to the opening letter of the word before it

blocks.note: fourteen letters taken as written
its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone dressed oddly casually draws a ticking-off.
explanation.definitionFit: Cautionary tales are stories told to warn, so they amount to admonitory messages.

clue.text: Was humiliated in café?

blocks.note: surface reading: someone was embarrassed while out at a coffee shop
setter's reading: the word café is what you get when a facial word has lost its order, its letters jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone suffered an embarrassment in a coffee shop.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as wordplay: FACE gone astray, scrambled, makes CAFE. The question mark warns that the clue works backwards from the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To lose face is the idiom for suffering humiliation or loss of dignity in front of others.

clue.text: Greedy types reported in Prince's domain

indicators.note: what is reported is passed on by word of mouth, so the sound of the word counts

blocks.note: whales are gluttonous eaters, and in casinos big spenders

explanation.surface: Gluttons are said to be found in the Prince's realm.
explanation.walkthrough: The Prince of Wales is the title of the British heir to the throne, so Wales is his nominal principality.
explanation.definitionFit: The country is the principality from which the heir to the British throne takes his title.

clue.text: Sweetheart losing head over former sweetheart's heartless malediction? I'm not buying it

definitions.note: a phrase you say to a feeble justification, not a noun

indicators.note: losing its head means the first letter is dropped
heartless means the central letter is taken out

blocks.note: an old flame is a former lover; a flame is a sweetheart
an ex is a former partner
a malediction is a curse

explanation.surface: A beheaded lover hurls a heartless curse at a former partner, and the listener is unconvinced.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' means placed above, so the pieces simply follow in order. The definition is the listener's retort rather than a dictionary synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: A feeble, unconvincing justification is the thing a sceptical listener is refusing to accept when saying the quoted words.

clue.text: Trusted friends at college begin here

definitions.note: a place where you start, not a verb phrase

blocks.note: your main men are your closest, most trusted friends
U is short for university

explanation.surface: Close friends at university start their adventure here.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'begin here' as the label a screen might show: it is where a user starts navigating software.
explanation.definitionFit: The top-level screen of a program or website is the starting point from which every other option is chosen.

clue.text: Meat from wild animals, not named at first

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so the letters run loose into a new order
not tells you to leave something out of the word before it
at first points to the opening letter of the preceding word

blocks.note: taken as written
its first letter

explanation.surface: Some unidentified meat has come from wild beasts.
explanation.definitionFit: Salami is a cured, spiced sausage, so it is a kind of preserved meat.

clue.text: Actress reportedly to bear chess prodigy

indicators.note: reportedly means as people say it, so both parts are taken by sound

blocks.note: to bear a load is to carry it
Bobby Fischer was the American chess prodigy and world champion

explanation.surface: An actress is said to be pregnant with a future chess genius.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bear' looks like giving birth, but it means carry; both halves are sound-alikes.
explanation.definitionFit: She was the American performer who played Princess Leia in Star Wars, so she is an example of an actress.

clue.text: Humongous T. rex demolished a brewed lager

indicators.note: something demolished is knocked down and its pieces scattered
brewing mixes ingredients up, so these letters are stirred into a new order

blocks.note: the letters of the dinosaur's name
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A huge dinosaur wrecked a freshly brewed beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Humongous is slang for enormous, and the answer is the clothing-size term for very big.

clue.text: Germanic invader beheaded – some nerve!

indicators.note: a beheaded word loses its head, its first letter

blocks.note: the Saxons were a Germanic people who invaded Britain

explanation.surface: A decapitated invader, and the exclamation marks the cheek of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some nerve!' sounds like outrage at audacity; it really means part of a nerve.
explanation.definitionFit: An axon is the long fibre of a nerve cell, so it is a part of a nerve.

clue.text: For a special occasion, taking tea? I don't think so!

indicators.note: taking something in means holding it within, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: a nonce word is one coined for a single special occasion; 'for the nonce' means for the time being
cha (or char) is informal British for tea

explanation.surface: Someone is asked whether they'll have tea on a special occasion, and declines.
explanation.walkthrough: Nonce means the present or a particular occasion, as in a nonce word, invented for one use.
explanation.definitionFit: Both the exclamation and the answer are emphatic refusals, conveying that something will not happen.

clue.text: Fictional relative's tuna-salad-and-cracker-eating bird

indicators.note: a salad is a mixture tossed together, so these letters are tossed into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, to be mixed
'Polly wants a cracker' is the stock line given to a pet parrot

explanation.surface: A relative's parrot eats a tuna salad with crackers.
explanation.walkthrough: Aunt Polly is Tom Sawyer's guardian aunt in Mark Twain's novels.
explanation.definitionFit: She is the aunt who raises Tom Sawyer in Twain's books, so she is a relative from fiction.

clue.text: Greta munches a Pacific nation's bean

indicators.note: what you munch goes into your mouth, so the first piece takes the rest inside

blocks.note: Greta Garbo was the Swedish film star
taken as written
NZ is the abbreviation for New Zealand

explanation.surface: Greta eats a bean from a country in the Pacific.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greta' looks like the activist; it is the screen star.
explanation.definitionFit: Garbanzo is the Spanish-derived name for the chickpea, which is a kind of legume.

clue.text: Feudal drudge returns with mop that's not found in big cities

definitions.text: that's not found in big cities
definitions.note: a descriptive phrase standing in for the noun

indicators.note: something that returns goes back, so the word is read from end to start

blocks.note: a serf was a labourer bound to a feudal lord
a mop is a thick head of hair

explanation.surface: A medieval peasant comes back with a mop, something rare in a metropolis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mop' suggests cleaning, but it is a shock of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Clean, unpolluted outdoor atmosphere is what crowded, traffic-filled urban areas are known to lack.

clue.text: Feature of retrograde love song

indicators.note: of here means taken from within, so the letters sit inside the words that follow
retrograde means moving backwards, so the run of letters is read in reverse

blocks.note: the letters spanning the gap between the two words

explanation.surface: A characteristic of an old-fashioned romantic ballad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retrograde' passes for old-fashioned; it really sends the hidden letters backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The nose is one of the parts of a face, which are called features.

clue.text: Lyrical author followed by jerk

blocks.note: Edgar Allan Poe, the American writer
a tic is an involuntary twitch or jerk

explanation.surface: An expressive writer is being trailed by an obnoxious person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jerk' looks like an insult, but it is a twitch.
explanation.definitionFit: Lyrical writing is expressive and imaginative, the quality of verse, so the two adjectives are synonyms.

clue.text: Fare with a pea in each part, I hear – or a lot of them?

definitions.text: Fare with a pea in each part, I hear – or a lot of them?

blocks.clueFragment: Fare with a pea in each part
blocks.note: surface reading: a dish with a vegetable in every portion

blocks.clueFragment: a pea in each part, I hear
blocks.note: setter's reading: the sound of a pea is the letter P, and each of the two words of the dish contains one
the dish is full of letters, P among them

explanation.surface: A meal with peas in every portion, or maybe heaps of them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A pea' is the letter P said out loud: both words of the answer contain a P, and the soup itself is full of pasta letters.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a broth with small pasta shapes of the letters, so it is a dish full of characters.

clue.text: Creature sounding like a buzzard, they say

indicators.note: they say means as people pronounce it, so a sound-alike is wanted

blocks.note: a voice that rasps like a bird's harsh cry is gravelly and husky

explanation.surface: An animal whose call resembles a bird of prey's, so people claim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sounding like' seems to be the sound-alike signal, but it describes the rasping voice; 'they say' does the homophone work.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse is an animal, so it is an example of a creature.

clue.text: King Charlie in bind

blocks.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
a charlie is British slang for a fool, as is nit

explanation.surface: King Charles finds himself in a tight spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'King Charlie' looks like the monarch; Charlie is slang for an idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: To knit can mean to join or bind together, as broken bones knit or brows knit.

clue.text: One who won't drink and drive, in practice

blocks.note: a dry is a teetotaller
to run a car or a business is to drive it

explanation.surface: A teetotaller who drives, as a habit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In practice' reads as 'habitually'; 'practice' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A rehearsal or trial run is a practice before the real event.

clue.text: Rent by oneself for much less

blocks.note: to let a property is to rent it out
being by oneself is being alone

explanation.surface: Renting solo costs a lot less.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Much less' sounds like a cheaper price; it is the phrase 'not to mention'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases introduce something even less likely, as in 'he can't walk, much less run'.

clue.text: Words of daring, say, embraced by champions

indicators.note: something embraced by another is held within its arms

blocks.note: heroes are champions
e.g. means for example, that is, say

explanation.surface: Brave words, perhaps, from those hugged by the winners.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is what someone says on summoning the nerve to attempt something risky.

clue.text: Modern currency? Scream 'opt out!'

indicators.note: out as in out of order, so the word's letters are rearranged

blocks.note: a cry is a scream
taken as written, to be jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone yells at people to withdraw from a newfangled money system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opt out' looks like a single phrase; 'out' is detached as the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The short form refers to cryptocurrency, digital money such as Bitcoin, a recent kind of currency.
